question.text: In an LLP-form AIF used in many foreign jurisdictions (and permitted in India), the Manager is typically referred to as the _______ and the investors are referred to as the _______.

explanation.text: The Logic: In the LLP structure, the manager is referred to as the General Partner (GP) and the investors as Limited Partners (LPs). GP holds management rights and unlimited decision-making authority; LPs are passive capital providers with liability limited to their commitment. The Trap: Options A, B, D mix up terminology from the trust form (sponsor, settlor, trustee, unitholder) or are fabricated. Cross-Exam Context: Shared across XIX-A/B/C/D. PE/VC-heavy Cat I/II XIX-D frames drawdown mechanics around GP-LP; Cat III uses GP-LP only if LLP form chosen. Manager's Pro-Tip: For Cat III in an LLP form, remember the 'GP catch-up' and 'hurdle waterfall' common in Cat I/II are rare — Cat III uses HWM crystallisation on NAV, so the GP-LP economics look different from a classic PE LLP.
